overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation for the February 2 or February 16 meetings: the chair did not reasonably anticipate the property discussions when notices were posted. Other allegations were declined or fell outside the law.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Commission failed to list discussion of the complainants' property on its February 2 meeting notice.
allegations.key_passage: We therefore find that the Commission chair did not reasonably anticipate discussing this issue 48 hours in advance of the February 2 meeting, and the Commission therefore did not violate the Open Meeting Law by failing to include this discussion from the meeting notice.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Commission failed to list discussion of the complainants' property on its February 16 meeting notice, which was revised on the day of the meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Because the Commission chair could not have anticipated discussing the property at issue at the time the notice was posted, we find that the Commission did not violate the Open Meeting Law with respect to this allegation.

allegations.summary: Complaints alleged the Conservation Director made untrue statements during a meeting; the AG declined to review as not an Open Meeting Law issue.
allegations.key_passage: Because these allegations do not constitute violations of the Open Meeting Law, we decline to review them.

allegations.summary: Complaints alleged residents who were the subject of a Commission discussion did not receive individualized notice; the AG declined to review.
allegations.key_passage: Because these allegations do not constitute violations of the Open Meeting Law, we decline to review them.

allegations.summary: One complainant alleged a Commission secretary's February 9 email misinformed him about when a property would be discussed.
allegations.key_passage: We note that the secretary is an individual town employee and is not a public body subject to the Open Meeting Law.
